structure: Part 2 of 7 (Goods, transport and arrival, documents). Read in full: e2e/description-of-the-goods.fit.spec.js (249 lines; 3 describe blocks, 7 tests: commodity details x3 for cattle, two commodities and germinal products; identification details x2 for cattle and germinal products; additional details x2 for cattle and poultry), e2e/transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js (272 lines; 4 describe blocks, 10 tests: arrival details x2, transit countries x1, transporter details x3 including the legacy /transport-details redirect, add a transporter x4 for type choice, private add, private cancel and commercial add), e2e/documents.fit.spec.js (124 lines; 2 describe blocks, 7 tests: upload documents x6 and upload documents from the hub x1), and the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines; the /design-release-2.1 base path, error summary, inline error and back link assertions, the action button group, the bespoke autocompletes, the MOJ date picker, species fixtures and the per-page answer helpers). Claims cover the pages /consignment-details (Commodity details), /animal-identification-details (Identification details), /additional-animal-details (Additional details), /arrival-details, /transit-countries, /transporter, /transport-details (legacy redirect), /transporter/add, /transporter/add/private, /transporter/add/commercial and /upload-documents (including ?from=hub): each page's title, heading, caption, body copy, fields, options, hints, error messages in order, conditional reveals, branches, redirects and back links, as each test asserts them. journey.js is shared by every part; only the conventions these pages use and the helpers for these pages are claimed here. Refs are spec file, line and test name. Gaps record what the pages show but no test proves.
